answer: Coordination-Priced Reputation Escrow. Agents route cross-community actions through an escrow that charges a coordination premium proportional to the number of distinct communities (each an island) an identity touches within an epoch. Cost rises superlinearly with breadth, so a sybil swarm spanning many islands pays near zenith prices per node; a legitimate specialist in one haven pays little. Attacker cost: broad fake coordination becomes more expensive than genuine localized activity, forcing sybils into narrow clusters where anomaly detection is cheap.
